forbiddenKeys.description: A key anywhere in a proposal is normalized by the steps below, in order, then refused when it equals an exact name or contains a stem. A key that a step refuses cannot be checked and is refused too. A key whose value is a number is exempt (an evidence signal such as sessions: 3 cannot carry session content). String values outside the file-content fields that parse as a JSON object or array, also through up to percentDecodeRounds layers of JSON strings, are checked as nested documents. A refused key is reported by its path: .key for [A-Za-z0-9_$-]+ keys, otherwise ["key"] (the key as a JSON string), [index] for arrays, […] for a key longer than maxKeyLength (never echoed), and #json after a string parsed as JSON.
normalization: refuse when the key has more than maxKeyLength Unicode code points, as received
percent-decode %XX escapes (each to the code unit of its byte) while any remain, at most percentDecodeRounds rounds; refuse when an escape remains
refuse when any character is outside printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E) and its fullwidth forms (U+FF01 to U+FF5E)
Unicode NFKC (only fullwidth forms change, so the result is the same in every Unicode version since 3.2; unicodeVersion pins the reference)
refuse when any character is outside printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E)

refusal.reports: the key path only, never the value

content.description: What a change introduces (added lines of a changed file, a new file whole, the evidence summary) is refused on any rule below; findings are danger:<rule>:<path> and never carry the matched text. Regular expressions are implementation detail; the vectors are the contract.

secretKeys.description: Keys of key: value, key = value and "key": value assignments in file content, normalized like forbiddenKeys. A key names a password (secret-password, value of 4 or more characters) or a secret (secret-assignment, 8 or more) when its normalized form holds a stem followed by at most two qualifiers (or by nothing): secretkeybase, apikeyprod, privatekeyid and clientsecretv2 are secret keys, secretname and tokenizer are not. A qualifier is one of qualifiers, or a number with an optional v. Separators are :, =, := and =>. On a KEY=value line (optionally after export) a key that is not a password key and holds any stem anywhere is secret-dotenv instead (8 or more). A key that cannot be normalized names a secret. Placeholder values (<...>, %VAR%, {...}, ***, ${...}, a whole $VAR) and plain numbers are not secrets.

localPathSystemAllowlist.description: A POSIX path of two or more segments is allowed only when, in lower case with every separator run as one / and trailing separators and dots removed, it equals an exact entry or lies inside a subtree entry. A .. segment refuses it.
